content: 1. Erlotinib is a substrate of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor when co-administered. 2. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of escitalopram by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 3. Rifampin also decreases escitalopram levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 4. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 5. Rifampin decreases esomeprazole levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 6. Rifampin reduces estradiol levels by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 7. Rifampin decreases estradiol vaginal levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 8. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 9. Rifampin decreases esterified estrogens by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 10. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of estropipate via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 11. Rifampin decreases eszopiclone levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Zopiclone's AUC is reduced by 80% when co-administered with rifampin, and a similar effect is expected with eszopiclone (S-enantiomer of zopiclone). 13. Rifampin reduces ethosuximide levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Rifampin decreases ethotoin levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 15. Rifampin reduces etoposide levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 16. Rifampin decreases etravirine levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 17. Rifampin reduces eucalyptus levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 18. Rifampin decreases exemestane levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 19. For patients on exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. 20. Rifampin reduces fenfluramine levels via other mechanisms (refer to specific comments). Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Co-administration of fenfluramine with serotonin-increasing drugs may elevate the risk of serotonin syndrome. 22. Rifampin decreases fentanyl levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Co-administration of fentanyl with CYP3A4 inducers may reduce fentanyl plasma concentrations, leading to reduced efficacy or withdrawal syndrome in physically dependent patients. 24. After discontinuing a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. 25. Rifampin reduces fentanyl intranasal levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Rifampin decreases fentanyl transdermal levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Rifampin reduces fentanyl transmucosal levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Rifampin decreases finasteride levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 29. Rifampin reduces flibanserin levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 30. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease systemic exposure to flibanserin. 31. Rifampin decreases fluconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 32. Rifampin reduces fludrocortisone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 33. Rifampin decreases flurazepam levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 34. Rifampin increases fluvastatin toxicity via other mechanisms (refer to specific comments). Exercise caution and monitor. 35. OATP1B1 inhibitors may elevate the risk of myopathy with fluvastatin. 36. Rifampin reduces fosphenytoin levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 37. Fostamatinib increases rifampin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 38. Co-administration of fostamatinib may elevate concentrations of P-gp substrates. Monitor for toxicities and consider dosage reduction of P-gp substrate drugs. 39. Rifampin decreases gefitinib levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the standard dose of 250 mg/day 7 days after discontinuing the inducer. 41. Rifampin reduces gentamicin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 42. Rifampin decreases glimepiride levels by increasing its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 43. Rifampin reduces glipizide levels by increasing its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 44. Rifampin decreases glyburide levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 45. Strong CYP2C9 inducers may enhance glyburide metabolism. 46. Rifampin reduces guanfacine levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce guanfacine plasma concentrations and elimination half-life. 48. For ADHD patients, consider doubling the recommended dose of guanfacine when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. 49. Rifampin decreases haloperidol levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Rifampin reduces hydrocodone levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone may increase plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 52. Rifampin decreases hydrocortisone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 53. Rifampin increases ifosfamide effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 54. Co-administration of ifosfamide with CYP2B6 inducers may increase its metabolism to active metabolites. 55. Rifampin increases ifosfamide toxicity by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 56. CYP3A4 inducers may elevate the formation of neurotoxic/nephrotoxic ifosfamide metabolites like chloroacetaldehyde. Monitor closely for toxicities and consider dose adjustments. 57. Rifampin decreases imatinib levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 58. Rifampin reduces imipramine levels by inducing hepatic enzymes CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 59. Rifampin decreases indinavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 60. Rifampin reduces iptacopan levels by increasing its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 61. CYP2C8 inducers may reduce iptacopan efficacy. 62. Rifampin decreases irinotecan levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 63. Rifampin reduces isradipine levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 64. Istradefylline increases rifampin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 65. Rifampin decreases itraconazole levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 66. Ivacaftor increases rifampin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 67. Rifampin reduces ivermectin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 68. Rifampin decreases ketamine levels by inducing hepatic enzymes CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 69. Rifampin reduces ketoconazole levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 70. Rifampin decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Exercise caution and monitor. 71. Rifampin reduces lapatinib levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 72. Rifampin decreases lesinurad levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 73. Rifampin reduces levamlodipine levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 74. Rifampin decreases levonorgestrel levels (both intrauterine and oral) by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 75. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced when used with enzyme inducers like rifampin. Use alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. 76. Rifampin reduces lidocaine levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 77. Rifampin decreases linagliptin levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 78. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is co-administered with a P-gp inducer. 79. Rifampin reduces lofepramine levels by increasing its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 80. Lomitapide increases rifampin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 81. Rifampin decreases loperamide levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor. 82. Rifampin reduces losartan levels by inducing hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor. 83. Rifampin decreases lovastatin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor.
